Systems

Terrain & water

In critiqueround 4
Critic verdict
Round 3: TOSS-UP conf 3 — charm 7, readability 5, density 6, polish 4 (aerial beats FarmVille; water loses)
Biggest gap
The sea is still a flat matte gradient at the distances the game shows it (measured high-frequency detail 1.1–1.5 vs 26 on the frosting ground): wave normals/crests must survive to 30–120 u, with a sun-glint path, sky reflection, a shallow band at every shore and ripple rings at pilings/hulls.
Latest improvement
Round 3: LOD ripple stack + crest lines + albedo chop so the sea keeps detail at any distance (HF detail 0.85→2.4), sky-gradient reflection, glint road to the horizon, scalloped surf + shoal band, piling/ferry ripple rings, one sea palette; river gets a sugar-crust lip mesh, darker syrup, along-channel streaks, waterfall lip/spray/basin; glossy lake with caramel rim and darkened decks; village plaza pavers with sprinkle grout + kerb; pink zone desaturated; paw prints crisp; 13 meshes / 149k tris.
Remaining weaknesses (5)
  • Syrup river reads as a flat decal; streaks run across the flow
  • Chocolate lake fully matte, no rim; boardwalk same value as the lake
  • Frosting in the pink zone as saturated as the props; icing plateau brightest surface
  • Gumdrop Village square is a bare pink slab (no cobbles/wear/kerb)
  • Hard black shadows + no contact AO (sky/terrain)

Sky, lighting, day/night

In critiqueround 4
Critic verdict
Round 3: TOSS-UP conf 3 — charm 8, density 8, lighting 5, polish 4 (night cat street ≈8, dawn harbour 3)
Biggest gap
Night and dusk read as a global brightness multiply, not a change of light: unlit surfaces keep daytime saturation; needs a cool blue-violet moon key + cool ambient so unlit surfaces desaturate toward blue and warm lamps are the only saturated colour.
Latest improvement
Round 4: night is now a light change — a darkness-weighted sky wash (global shader patch) desaturates unlit surfaces toward blue, a real blue-violet moon key (3.0) with lower exposure, two-sided key/fill rig, noon key:fill 26:1 → 5.5:1 with warm bounce, fountain shadow bands gone (texel-based normalBias), dawn harbour re-aimed at the sun; value curve noon 116 > dusk 66 > night 46.
Remaining weaknesses (4)
  • Noon cast shadows are hard near-black stencils with no fill/AO
  • Dawn 05:53 harbour: no visible sun disc/horizon glow, no shadows
  • Three of five gameplay frames show no sky (camera pitch)
  • Stair-step tearing bands on the pink fountain tiers (shadow acne?)

Sour Patch Kids

In critiqueround 4
Critic verdict
Round 3: TOSS-UP conf 3 — charm 6, readability 5, polish 3, lighting 3 (night faces praised)
Biggest gap
The kids are opaque matte plastic with white splotch decals; they need a translucent gummy material with light through the limbs, a warm rim, and a crystalline specular sparkle layer that catches the sun as they move.
Latest improvement
Round 3: translucent gummy material (fresnel rim, baked thickness transmission, fine crystalline crust with sun-facing glints + 3–6 sprite twinkles per kid), true Sour-Patch silhouette (flat-topped head, neck, splayed nubs), brightest-pixel night eyes with halo, stronger contact blobs, dancers actually at the fountain + village sunbather + dusk freeze facing the player, continuous salt ridge with clustered crystals; 9–14 draw calls.
Remaining weaknesses (5)
  • Night eyes are the darkest pixels, not emissive at distance
  • No contact shadows on kids
  • Pose library reads as two poses; dusk stare beat not visible
  • Salt line reads as broken glass, not a ridge
  • Night only 26% darker than midday; dusk twice as dark as night (sky)
